text:
katy: Quick idea — what if we add a lease-less "soft" eviction fallback for tiny tenants during bursty reads? Reduce lease churn and avoid hot rebalancing during short spikes.
ravi: I like that. Sketch: keep a per-tenant soft token balance + hysteresis. Evict markers are local and ephemeral; only escalate to full lease eviction when balance depleted or write activity seen.
marcus: Curious about correctness here. If we drop leases we might return stale reads or violate RAWR for active cursors. How do we gate reads after a soft-evict?
ravi: Two parts: 1) soft-evict only affects cache residency, not primary store ownership. Reads fall back to authoritative read path when cache miss. 2) include an evict_marker with idempotency so handoffs/replicas ignore duplicate evicts. Example marker: `evict_marker: "tenant-<id>-<epoch>-<seq>"`
jen: But what about write-after-evict races? If a client writes immediately after we soft-evict, a subsequent read could get a stale cached value if the cache rehydrates incorrectly.
ravi: Right — require a lightweight validation step on rehydrate if there was a recent soft-evict for that prefix. We can keep a small per-prefix generation number in metadata and check on rehydrate; if mismatch, force authoritative fetch.
katy: Can we express the config simply? Something like:
```
evict_policy:
  mode: leaseless_soft
  soft_quota_tokens: 10000
  hysteresis_pct: 20
  cooldown_s: 30
```
marcus: That looks clean. We should also surface per-tenant policy flags so platform can opt-in high-priority tenants to always use real leases. e.g. `rr set tenant:acme evict_policy=lease` — routing-level override.
ops-bot: metric alert — evict_soft_count increased 4.1x in the last surge window for node-gpu-12 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
jen: Ops data is useful. We should add telemetry for: soft_evict_count, rehydrate_forced_count, rejected_rehydrate_count, and avg_rehydrate_latency.
ravi: Edge case: prefix handoff during concurrent soft-evict can cause double removal. Idempotency markers handle this but we should also make cleanup convergent: garbage collect stale markers after `marker_ttl`.
katy: Testing plan: small canary (5% traffic) with canary tenants marked leaseless_soft, run traffic generator with mixed read/write patterns for 48h, watch RAWR regressions and rehydrate rates.
jen: Add smoke tests that simulate immediate write after soft-evict and ensure read path returns authoritative value. Also test long-lived cursors and cursor-resume across soft-evict.
marcus: Ops concern: cost — this may increase backend reads during storms. Need threshold math so cost/regression tradeoff is explicit in the config (token burn -> escalate).
katy: OK — next steps: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with config examples, telemetry spec, and rollout plan. Can someone volunteer to own the canary harness?
ravi: I can prototype the token-based balancer + marker format.
marcus: I can own the canary harness and dashboards.
jen: I'll write the smoke tests and validation scenarios.
katy: great, thanks everyone. Filing RFC follow-up + checklist today. :thumbsup:
